differential.name: Advanced diabetic nephropathy (chronic kidney disease stage 4)

supporting_evidence.finding: History of type 2 diabetes >15 years with progressive rise in serum creatinine

differential.reasoning: Long‑standing diabetes with markedly reduced eGFR and proteinuria is classic for advanced diabetic nephropathy, accounting for the majority of the patient's renal dysfunction.

differential.name: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease

supporting_evidence.finding: Documented prior myocardial infarction and ongoing angina equivalents
Elevated LDL cholesterol (value pending) and high cardiovascular risk profile

differential.reasoning: Prior MI and risk factors (diabetes, dyslipidaemia) make obstructive CAD the most plausible atherosclerotic cause of current symptoms.

differential.name: Hypertension

supporting_evidence.finding: History of hypertension with intermittent medication adjustments
Absence of recent blood pressure measurements noted

differential.reasoning: Uncontrolled or poorly documented blood pressure likely contributes to CKD progression and cardiovascular risk.

differential.name: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)

supporting_evidence.finding: Dyspnea on exertion and peripheral edema without reduced EF documented

differential.reasoning: Symptoms compatible with HFpEF in a hypertensive, diabetic patient, but lack of echocardiography limits certainty.

differential.name: Non‑alcoholic fatty liver disease / non‑alcoholic steatohepatitis (NAFLD/NASH)

supporting_evidence.finding: Obesity, dyslipidaemia, and elevated ALT/AST (values pending)

differential.reasoning: Metabolic syndrome components raise suspicion for NAFLD/NASH, though imaging confirmation is lacking.

differential.name: Chronic kidney disease‑Mineral Bone Disorder (CKD‑MBD)

supporting_evidence.finding: Elevated phosphate and secondary hyperparathyroidism (values pending)
Stage 4 CKD present, predisposing to mineral bone disease

differential.reasoning: Advanced CKD commonly leads to disturbances in calcium‑phosphate metabolism and bone turnover.

differential.name: Metformin‑associated lactic acidosis (early/sub‑clinical)
differential.reasoning: While metformin can precipitate lactic acidosis in renal impairment, lack of lactate data makes this diagnosis unlikely.

differential.name: Diabetic autonomic neuropathy (including impaired urinary concentrating ability)
differential.reasoning: Dilute urine may be due to CKD‑related concentrating defect rather than autonomic neuropathy.

differential.name: Major depressive disorder / anxiety

supporting_evidence.finding: Patient reports low mood and worry, but no formal screening completed

differential.reasoning: Psychiatric symptoms are possible but lack validated assessment tools.

differential.name: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)
differential.reasoning: High prevalence in this phenotype, yet no objective testing performed.

primary_diagnosis: Advanced diabetic nephropathy (chronic kidney disease stage 4)
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient’s long‑standing type 2 diabetes with markedly reduced eGFR and proteinuria makes advanced diabetic nephropathy the dominant diagnosis. Co‑existing atherosclerotic CAD is strongly supported by prior MI and cardiovascular risk factors. Hypertension, HFpEF, and CKD‑MBD are logical sequelae of the renal disease and metabolic syndrome. Remaining entities (NAFLD/NASH, metformin‑associated lactic acidosis, autonomic neuropathy, mood disorder, OSA) are plausible but have limited objective data, reflected in lower probabilities.
unresolved_findings: Absence of recent blood pressure measurements – needed to confirm hypertension control.
Missing lipid panel and HbA1c values – limits assessment of dyslipidaemia and glycaemic control.
No arterial lactate measurement – prevents definitive exclusion or confirmation of metformin‑associated lactic acidosis.
Lack of echocardiographic data – cannot confirm or exclude HFpEF or quantify cardiac function.
No liver imaging or FibroScan – NAFLD/NASH remains presumptive.
No formal mental‑health screening (PHQ‑9, GAD‑7) – depression/anxiety not quantified.
No sleep study – OSA remains speculative.
Bone‑mineral labs (PTH, calcium, phosphate, vitamin D) not available – CKD‑MBD not fully characterized.
recommended_workup: Serum lactate level to rule out metformin‑associated lactic acidosis.
Comprehensive metabolic panel including calcium, phosphate, PTH, vitamin D.
Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring or clinic BP measurement.
Echocardiogram with diastolic function assessment and BNP measurement for HFpEF evaluation.
Liver ultrasound or FibroScan to assess NAFLD/NASH.
Urine albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio for quantifying proteinuria.
